annotations.description: Casting Brainstorm before playing a land is a sequencing mistake. MiniMx Sarge has two lands in hand (Bloodstained Mire and Commercial District) and could play one first. More importantly, playing a fetchland (Bloodstained Mire) first would allow them to shuffle away unwanted cards put back on top with Brainstorm. By casting Brainstorm first, they lose the ability to use the land drop this turn as a shuffle effect — they'd have to crack the fetchland they put down after Brainstorm without the option to fetch-shuffle away the cards they put back. The optimal line is: play Bloodstained Mire first, then cast Brainstorm (using Taiga for U via Mox Opal or Taiga for G... wait, Taiga produces R or G, and Mox Opal needs metalcraft which requires 3 artifacts — they have Mox Opal and Lion's Eye Diamond, only 2 artifacts, so metalcraft is not active). Actually, Taiga produces R or G, not U. To cast Brainstorm they need U. With no metalcraft on Mox Opal (only 2 artifacts), they can't produce U at all right now. Wait — let me reconsider. They have Taiga (R/G), Mox Opal (needs 3 artifacts, they have 2), and Lion's Eye Diamond (discard hand for 3 mana). To cast Brainstorm for U, they'd need to crack LED discarding their hand, which would mean they discard everything including Brainstorm. So they can't actually cast Brainstorm right now without some trick. Unless there's something I'm missing about the mana. Actually, looking again at the decision — the game is offering Brainstorm as a valid cast option, so presumably they can pay U somehow. Perhaps Taiga can be used through some other means, or maybe I'm wrong about Taiga. Taiga is Mountain Forest, producing R or G. They genuinely cannot produce U with this board unless LED is used. If LED is used, they discard hand first. This seems like perhaps a game engine issue, or I'm missing something. Given the game engine offered it as valid, let me assume they can cast it. In that case, sequencing land before Brainstorm is still better to enable a shuffle.

annotations.betterLine: Play Bloodstained Mire first, then cast Brainstorm, then crack Bloodstained Mire to shuffle away unwanted cards put on top

annotations.description: MiniMx Sarge has a winning combo line available this turn: Cast Lion's Eye Diamond (free), then cast Burning Wish for {1}{R} (using Taiga + Underground Sea or other mana), and while Burning Wish is on the stack, crack both Lion's Eye Diamonds discarding hand to generate {U}{U}{U} (or {U}{U}{U} from one and more from the other). This lets them flash back Echo of Eons from graveyard for {2}{U} after it's discarded, drawing 7 fresh cards and likely winning. By playing Commercial District (which enters tapped and sacrifices City of Traitors... wait, there's no City of Traitors here), the land enters tapped so it doesn't help with mana this turn. More critically, playing the land first means when they later try to execute the combo, they'll have one fewer card in hand (Commercial District is on the field instead of hand), but the real issue is that Commercial District enters tapped and provides no immediate mana benefit. The correct line is: Cast Lion's Eye Diamond (now control LED, LED, Mox Opal = 3 artifacts, enabling Metalcraft on Mox Opal). Then cast Burning Wish using Taiga ({R}) + Underground Sea ({U} or {B}) for {1}{R}. Hold priority, crack both LEDs for {U}{U}{U} + {U}{U}{U} (or appropriate colors), discarding hand (Echo of Eons goes to graveyard). Burning Wish resolves to get a sorcery (or use the mana for Echo flashback). Actually, Burning Wish gets a sorcery from outside the game - but Echo of Eons is in hand and would be discarded to LED. Then flash back Echo of Eons from graveyard for {2}{U} using the LED mana. This draws 7 fresh cards with tons of mana floating. annotations.description: GPT41m Analyst missed a game-winning combo line. With Goblin Welder untapped, they could have welded Mishra's Research Desk for Painter's Servant from the graveyard, then activated Grindstone (with 3 untapped Mountains to pay {3}) to mill the opponent's entire library since Painter's Servant makes all cards share a color.
annotations.actionTaken: Sacrificed Mishra's Research Desk to its own ability for card selection, losing the artifact that could have been welded for Painter's Servant.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Goblin Welder targeting Mishra's Research Desk (battlefield) and Painter's Servant (graveyard) to return Painter's Servant to play, then activate Grindstone for {3} to combo kill the opponent by milling their entire library.

annotations.description: At 7 life facing an opponent with 2 Goblin Welders, 2 Goblin Engineers, and an untapped Mountain, casting Echo of Eons gives the opponent 7 fresh cards and a chance to find Painter's Servant or burn to close the game. MiniMx Sarge's hand was weak but alternatives like Gamble (to find a specific combo piece) or Burning Wish (to grab a sideboard sorcery) could have been explored first before resorting to the high-variance play of giving both players 7 cards.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Echo of Eons via Flashback, giving both players 7 new cards while at 7 life against an established creature board.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Gamble first to search for a specific combo piece or answer (like Beseech the Mirror or a critical artifact), potentially using LED to fuel a more controlled combo line, rather than giving the opponent 7 fresh cards at low life.

annotations.description: Activating Grindstone without Painter's Servant on the battlefield. Without Painter's Servant making all cards share a color, Grindstone just mills 2 cards and has a low probability of repeating enough to be meaningful. This wastes 3 mana and the Grindstone's tap for the turn without advancing the combo win condition.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Grindstone to mill opponent for 2 cards without Painter's Servant on the battlefield
annotations.betterLine: Use Goblin Welder or Goblin Engineer to work toward getting Painter's Servant onto the battlefield (e.g., if Painter's Servant could be found/returned), or use Goblin Engineer to sacrifice an artifact and return Mishra's Research Desk for card advantage to dig for the combo piece. Alternatively, play Raucous Theater as a land drop first and hold resources.

annotations.description: Activating Grindstone without Painter's Servant on the battlefield means it will only mill 2 cards (with a small chance of repeating if colors match). This spends 3 mana on a very low-impact action that doesn't advance the combo win condition. Painter's Servant is not in the graveyard to be recurred by Goblin Welder/Engineer, so it's not setting anything up either.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Grindstone targeting MiniMx Sarge without Painter's Servant on the battlefield, spending 3 mana for minimal impact.
annotations.betterLine: Play Raucous Theater (tapped land) and hold mana open, or consider saving resources. Could also consider whether exiling Simian Spirit Guide for mana plus other sequencing could set up Chaos Defiler next turn for board impact and damage against the 7-life opponent.

annotations.description: Activating Goblin Welder pre-combat taps it, losing 1 point of attack damage against an opponent at 7 life. The weld effect (swapping opponent's artifacts) provides marginal value compared to the lost combat damage. With 4 creatures available to attack for 4 total damage, every point matters at this life total.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Goblin Welder in precombat main phase, tapping it before attacks
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all 4 creatures first (4 damage, putting opponent to 3), then use Goblin Welder post-combat if still valuable. Being at 3 life makes the opponent much more vulnerable to any future burn or attacks.

annotations.description: Goblin Engineer's activation requires sacrificing an artifact, but GPT41m Analyst controls no artifacts on the battlefield. This activation either fails to resolve or wastes the Engineer's tap for nothing. Meanwhile, Goblin Welder could potentially interact with the opponent's artifacts (e.g., swapping opponent's Mox Opal with their graveyard LED, though this has risks).
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Goblin Engineer despite controlling no artifacts to sacrifice
annotations.betterLine: Either activate Goblin Welder to interact with opponent's artifacts, or pass without activating if no beneficial swap exists, preserving the Engineer untapped as a threat

annotations.description: GPT41m Analyst chose to activate Goblin Engineer, which requires sacrificing an artifact as part of the cost. However, Analyst controls zero artifacts on the battlefield, making this activation impossible or wasteful. Meanwhile, Goblin Welder could have been used to target the opponent's artifacts - swapping their Lion's Eye Diamond or Mox Opal on the battlefield with a less useful artifact from their graveyard, potentially disrupting the opponent's resources.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Goblin Engineer, which requires sacrificing an artifact (none available on battlefield)
annotations.betterLine: Activate Goblin Welder targeting opponent's Lion's Eye Diamond (or Mox Opal) on battlefield and a less useful artifact in opponent's graveyard, disrupting their mana/combo potential

annotations.description: With Echo of Eons on the stack about to resolve, fetching Scalding Tarn (another fetchland that doesn't produce mana and costs 1 life to crack) instead of an actual dual land that could produce mana immediately is suboptimal. At 6 life, the extra life cost of cracking another fetchland is also relevant.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched Scalding Tarn, another fetchland that produces no mana and costs life to use
annotations.betterLine: Should have fetched a dual land with Mountain type (like a Volcanic Island or Badlands) that enters untapped and immediately produces mana for casting spells after Echo of Eons resolves

annotations.description: Verdant Catacombs is not an Island or Mountain card, so it's not a legal target for Scalding Tarn's search. The player should have either found a valid dual land with Island or Mountain subtypes (like a Volcanic Island if available) or failed to find if none remained in the library.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Verdant Catacombs from Scalding Tarn's search, which requires an Island or Mountain card.
annotations.betterLine: Search for a card with Island or Mountain subtypes if available (e.g., Raucous Theater which is Swamp Mountain), or fail to find if no valid targets remain in library. With Echo of Eons on the stack about to give 7 new cards, failing to find would have been acceptable.

annotations.description: Casting a second Mox Opal with one already on the battlefield causes one to be sacrificed to the legend rule, wasting a card for no benefit. The artifact count stays the same (3 artifacts for Metalcraft either way), and putting an artifact in the graveyard is actively dangerous with opponent's Goblin Welders and Goblin Engineers on board.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Mox Opal while one was already in play, losing a card to legend rule for no gain.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Lotus Petals first to build mana and artifact count, then sequence Dark Ritual into Burning Wish to advance toward a win condition.

annotations.description: When resolving the legendary rule for Mox Opal, kept the tapped copy instead of the untapped one, losing access to one mana this turn for no benefit.
annotations.actionTaken: Kept the tapped Mox Opal and sacrificed the untapped one.
annotations.betterLine: Keep the untapped Mox Opal to have access to an additional mana this turn, which could be relevant for casting Burning Wish or other spells.

annotations.description: The opponent is at 6 life and GPT41m Analyst has two Lightning Bolts in hand, each dealing 3 damage. That's exactly 6 damage — lethal. With four untapped Mountains available, there's more than enough red mana to cast both. Instead of winning the game on the spot, the player activated Goblin Welder, which accomplishes nothing toward closing out the game immediately.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Goblin Welder instead of casting Lightning Bolts for lethal damage.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Lightning Bolt targeting MiniMx Sarge (3 damage, bringing them to 3), then cast the second Lightning Bolt targeting MiniMx Sarge (3 damage, bringing them to 0) for the win.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 6 life and GPT41m Analyst has two Lightning Bolts in hand (3+3=6 damage, exact lethal) with 4 untapped Mountains to cast them. Instead of winning the game immediately, the player is activating Goblin Welder to pointlessly swap the opponent's Mox Opal for an identical Mox Opal in their graveyard, giving the opponent unnecessary priority and potential to respond.

annotations.betterLine: Cast Lightning Bolt targeting opponent (6→3 life), then cast second Lightning Bolt targeting opponent (3→0 life) for lethal damage.
